# dsh-phone-bridge
**Turn DeepSeek Harness (DSH) into something you can carry in your pocket** — a WeChat bot that talk
s to your DSH from anywhere, plus a plugin that reshapes the DSH web UI into a phone-shaped app.
中文说明 · Setup guide · **Phone app** · Pitfalls · **Usage boundary**
> ⚠️ **Personal use only.** This is a single-owner tool: one person, one bot, one conversation. It i
s **not** authorised for public services, group messaging, marketing, harassment, privacy invasion,
circumventing platform rules, or operating someone else's account — see docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md. You
are solely responsible for how you deploy it.
## What's inside
Two independent DSH plugins — use either one on its own.
### 1. `dsh-wechat-connect` — WeChat bridge
Runs on your server and long-polls the WeChat iLink bot gateway. Text, images, voice and files go bo
th ways, in **one single conversation** with **one single working directory** — the bot serves its o
wner and nobody else.

- **Send the bot a photo** → DSH reads it with vision tools. **Send a document** → DSH opens it.
- *
*Ask for a file** → the model writes `[[send:/abs/path]]` and the bridge uploads it back to the chat

.
- **Scheduled digest** — at a configured time every day, DSH researches the previous day's world +

AI news and pushes it as **both** a chat message and a Word document.
- **Self-healing** — the long
-poll loop rebuilds itself after any failure, and writes a heartbeat so an external watchdog can cat
ch the "process alive but wedged" case.
### 2. `dsh-mobile-ui` — phone layout for the DSH web UI
The shipped web surface is a three-column desktop layout; on a phone the composer hides behind the k
eyboard, the sidebar crushes the conversation to a sliver, and the settings page wraps every label o
ne character per line. This plugin injects a stylesheet plus a small script through the documented `
webserver/index-inject` seam — **no source edits, no dist patching**:
| Problem on a phone | What the plugin does |

| Left icon rail eats 56px, controls are 28px tall | Bottom tab bar, 44px touch targets |
| Keyboard

covers the composer | Layout height tracks `visualViewport` |
| Sidebar squeezes content to 132px |

Full-screen conversation drawer that auto-closes on pick |
| Settings crushes labels vertically | F

ull-screen single column, nav becomes a horizontal strip |
| Right sidebar opens with no way back |

A visible "← back to chat" button |
| iOS zooms the page on focus | 16px inputs |
| No home-screen a
pp | PWA manifest + PNG icons → **installs as an app** (own icon, full screen, no browser UI) |
> 📱 **It also becomes a real phone app** — no APK, no app store: Chrome → "Add to Home screen" gives
you a full-screen app icon, and the manifest's `start_url` can point at a short login link so it re
-authenticates itself. See docs/MOBILE-APP.md.

## Design notes
- **Single owner, single conversation.** The bridge keeps one working directory and one DSH session
— the shape the WeChat bot gateway is actually built around. No per-contact machinery to misconfigur

e.
- **No DSH forks or patches.** The phone layout rides the documented index-injection seam; the br

idge is a plain DSH plugin.
- **Clone, don't move.** When the plugin needs a button in a React-owned
subtree (bottom tabs, composer actions), it clones the original node and forwards clicks — React re

conciliation is never disturbed.
- **Three layers of keep-alive.** systemd restart on crash → in-plu
gin loop rebuild on failure → external heartbeat watchdog for the wedged-but-alive case.
## Known limits
- The bot is a **separate WeChat account**, not you: it only sees messages sent *to it*, and cannot

read your personal chats.
- It is built for one owner. Keep `allowFrom` set to your own WeChat id so

strangers who find the bot get ignored.
- Proactive pushes (the digest) need a `context_token` from

an inbound message, so you must message the bot once first.
- The iLink bot gateway is not a public
, versioned API; `channel_version` changes the upload response shape (the code handles both).
## License and usage boundary
MIT for the code. Usage is limited to **personal self-hosted use** — see docs/USAGE-BOUNDARY.md.
